speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ecthyma Gangrenosum

The patient's symptoms and history are not consistent with Ecthyma Gangrenosum, a condition caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia, which typically presents in immunocompromised individuals with necrotic, painful skin lesions. The patient's lesions are described as painless, nonpruritic papules on the abdomen in a previously healthy 2-year-old, which is a classic presentation of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH), particularly given the daycare exposure and family history of viral infections.
